claim: The Legislature meets in regular session every year on the Tuesday after the first Monday of January
quote: in regular session on the Tuesday after the first Monday of January of the year A.D., 1970, and annually thereafter

claim: Regular sessions run 125 calendar days in 1972 and every fourth year after (2024, 2028), and 90 calendar days in the other years
quote: such sessions shall be limited to a period of one hundred twenty-five (125) calendar days for regular 1972 session and every fourth year thereafter, but ninety (90) calendar days for every other regular session thereafter

claim: Each house may extend a session by 30 days with a two-thirds vote, with no limit on extensions
quote: may extend such limited session for a period of thirty (30) days with no limit on the number of extensions to each session

claim: A bill not returned within five days (Sundays excepted) becomes law; if adjournment prevents return, the governor has fifteen days (Sundays excepted) to veto
quote: unless the Governor shall veto it within fifteen (15) days (Sundays excepted) after it is presented to him

claim: A bill not returned within five days (Sundays excepted) of presentment becomes law during the session
quote: returned by the Governor within five (5) days (Sundays excepted) after it has been presented to him, it shall become a law in like manner as if he had signed it

claim: Each act sets its own effective date; this 2025 election act took effect on 1 January 2025 for its new runoff rule
quote: [From and after January 1, 2025, this section shall read as follows:]

claim: County officers, supervisors, justice court judges and constables are elected at the general state election every four years, beginning 2023, for four-year terms
quote: At the election in 2023, and every four (4) years thereafter, there shall be elected a Governor

claim: The general state election includes circuit and chancery clerks, sheriffs, coroners, assessors, surveyors, supervisors, justice court judges and constables
quote: clerks of the circuit and chancery courts of the several counties, as well as sheriffs, coroners, assessors, surveyors and members of the boards of supervisors, justice court judges and constables

claim: Officers elected at the general state election serve four-year terms
quote: All such officers shall hold their offices for a term of four (4) years, and until their successors are elected and qualified

claim: Since 1 January 2025 a candidate at the general state election needs a majority to win
quote: that receives a majority of votes cast for the office at the general election shall be elected

claim: If no one has a majority, the top two meet in a runoff four weeks later
quote: placed on the ballot for the runoff election to be held four (4) weeks later

claim: Laws 2025, HB 291 was aimed at county and county district officers (title: require all candidates in the state general election to secure a majority)
quote: TO REQUIRE ALL CANDIDATES RUNNING IN THE STATE GENERAL ELECTION TO SECURE THE MAJORITY VOTE TO BE ELECTED

claim: The general election is held on the Tuesday after the first Monday of November
quote: A general election for all elective officers shall be held on the Tuesday next after the first Monday of November

claim: State and county party primaries are on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of August, with a second primary four weeks later
quote: The first primary shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of August preceding any regular or general election

claim: Ranked-choice voting is banned in statewide, county, local, municipal and school district elections
quote: TO PROHIBIT RANKED-CHOICE VOTING IN STATEWIDE, COUNTY, LOCAL, MUNICIPAL OR SCHOOL DISTRICT ELECTIONS

claim: A primary candidate needs a majority; otherwise the top two go to the second primary, where the most votes wins
quote: The candidate that receives a majority of the votes cast in the election shall be the party nominee

claim: A voter may vote in only one party primary on a given day
quote: No person shall vote or attempt to vote in the primary election of one (1) party when he or she has voted on the same date in the primary election of another party

claim: A voter who voted in one party first primary may not vote in another party second primary
quote: No person shall vote or attempt to vote in the second primary election of one (1) party when he or she has voted in the first primary election of another party

claim: The Legislature must secure fairness in party primaries
quote: The Legislature shall enact laws to secure fairness in party primary elections, conventions, or other methods of naming party candidates

claim: County and supervisor-district independents get on the ballot by petition filed with the circuit clerk
quote: shall be filed with the proper circuit clerk

claim: An independent appears on the ballot as an independent candidate
quote: he or she shall be listed on the ballot as an independent candidate

claim: Independent petitions must be signed by qualified electors of the county or supervisors district
quote: For an office elected by the qualified electors of a supervisors district

claim: A general municipal election is held in each city, town or village on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of June, every four years from 1985
quote: A general municipal election shall be held in each city, town or village on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of June 1985, and every four (4) years thereafter

claim: Municipal primaries are on the first Tuesday in April, with any second primary on the fourth Tuesday in April (moved from May by Laws 2017, HB 467)
quote: April preceding the general municipal election and, in the event a second primary shall be necessary, such second primary shall be held on the

claim: Municipal first primaries are on the first Tuesday of the month
quote: Municipal primary elections shall be held on the first Tuesday in

claim: The municipal second primary is on the fourth Tuesday in April
quote: April preceding such general municipal election

claim: A special or private charter municipality that declined the state schedule by 25 June 1952 holds its elections when its charter says
quote: shall not apply to any municipality operating under a special or private charter where the governing board or authority thereof, on or before June 25, 1952

claim: In those charter municipalities the primaries and general election are held at the time fixed by the charter
quote: in which event the primary and general elections shall be held at the time fixed by the charter of the municipality

claim: Municipal officers take office on the first weekday of July after the election, for four-year terms
quote: shall hold their offices for a term of four (4) years and until their successors are duly elected and qualified

claim: Municipal officers start on the first day of July after the general election that is not on a weekend
quote: enter upon the discharge of their duties on the first day of July after such general election that is not on a weekend

claim: Party nominations for all elective municipal offices are made in primaries
quote: Nominations for all municipal officers which are elective shall be made at a primary election, or elections

claim: A municipal candidate cannot qualify with a party that has no organized municipal executive committee
quote: No candidate may attempt to qualify with any political party that does not have a duly organized mun

claim: Municipal independents get on the ballot by petition filed with the municipal clerk and are listed as independents
quote: not having been nominated by a political party, shall have been requested to be a candidate for any office by a petition filed with the clerk of the municipality

claim: Municipal independents are listed on the ballot as independent candidates
quote: In the event such candidate qualifies as an independent as herein provided, he or she shall be listed on the ballot as an independent candidate

claim: Municipal general elections have no runoff (code charter municipalities); special charter municipalities follow their charters
citation: Secretary of State, 2026 County Election Handbook, p. 11 n.1
quote: There are no municipal general election runoffs

claim: Council-manager municipalities elect a mayor and councilmen
quote: At all elections held to choose a mayor and councilmen

claim: In council-manager cities the person with the highest number of votes is elected
quote: deliver to each person receiving the highest number of votes a certificate of election

claim: Judicial offices under the nonpartisan judicial election law include county court judge and justice court judge
quote: family court judge and justice court judge

claim: Judicial candidates may not align with any political party during a campaign
quote: to align himself or herself with any candidate or candidates for any other office or with any political faction or any political party at any time during any primary or general election campaign

claim: Justice court judges are elected on a nonpartisan basis from single-member districts set by the board of supervisors
quote: single member election districts in the county for the nonpartisan election of each of the justice court judges

claim: Judicial candidates need a majority at the general election, otherwise there is a runoff
quote: If any candidate for such an office receives a majority of the votes cast for such office in the general election, he shall be declared elected

claim: Judicial candidates go straight to the general election ballot
quote: If two (2) or more candidates qualify for judicial office, the names of those candidates shall be placed on the general election ballot

claim: Each county elects five election commissioners, one from each supervisors district, for four-year terms
quote: shall consist of one (1) person from each supervisor's district of the county

claim: From 2028, Districts One, Three and Five elect commissioners in 2028 and every four years after; Districts Two and Four from 2030
quote: At the general election in 2028 and every four (4) years thereafter, the qualified electors of the board of supervisors' Districts One, Three and Five

claim: Election commissioner candidates qualify by petition and their party affiliation, if any, is shown on the ballot
quote: All candidates shall declare in writing their party affiliation, if any, to the board of supervisors, and such party affiliation shall be shown on the official ballot

claim: Election commissioners list party affiliations but do not take part in primaries
citation: Secretary of State, 2026 County Election Handbook, p. 11
quote: do not participate in primaries, and are elected in the November General

claim: School board and school trustee candidates run as nonpartisan candidates in the November general election only
citation: Secretary of State, 2026 County Election Handbook, p. 11
quote: County School Board, Consolidated/Consolidated Line School District Trustee, Municipal

claim: Those candidates have no party designation on the ballot
citation: Secretary of State, 2026 County Election Handbook, p. 11
quote: designation of a political party affiliation on the ballot or otherwise

claim: Municipal primaries were moved from May to April by Laws 2017, HB 467 (the deleted word May is struck in the act)
quote: may april preceding the general municipal election

claim: County board of education members are elected by supervisors district
quote: members of the board from Supervisors Districts Three and Four

claim: Districts Two and Four elect commissioners in 2030 and every four years after
quote: At the general election in 2030 and every four (4) years thereafter

claim: County board of education members are elected for six-year terms at the regular general election in November
quote: all subsequent members of the board shall be elected for a term of six (6) years at the regular general election

claim: School trustee elections are held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each year, with a runoff four weeks later
quote: All such elections shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each year

claim: Since 2024, runoffs for state and county primaries, the general state election, judicial races and school trustee races are four weeks after the first election, not three
quote: TO REVISE THE TIME FOR HOLDING RUNOFF ELECTIONS TO FOUR WEEKS AFTER THE FIRST ELECTION INSTEAD OF THREE WEEKS

claim: School trustee candidates qualify by nominating petition filed with the county registrar
quote: a petition of nomination signed by not less than fifty (50) qualified electors of the school district

claim: Municipal separate school district boards have five members with five-year terms by default
quote: shall consist of five (5) members, each to be chosen for a term of five (5) years

claim: By default the city governing authorities choose those trustees; trustees for added territory outside the city are elected
quote: shall be elected by a majority of the governing authorities of the municipality

claim: In some mayor-council cities the trustees are appointed by the mayor and confirmed by the council
quote: to be appointed by the mayor and confirmed by the city council

claim: Each county is divided into five districts, each electing one member of the board of supervisors
quote: Each county shall be divided into five districts, a resident freeholder of each district shall be selected

claim: The five members constitute the board of supervisors
quote: the five so chosen shall constitute the board of supervisors of the county

claim: The chancery clerk is the clerk of the board of supervisors
quote: The clerk of the chancery court shall be the clerk of the board of supervisors

claim: Voters of each supervisors district elect one supervisor every four years
quote: The qualified electors of each district shall elect, at the next general election, and every four (4) years thereafter, in their districts one (1) member of the board of supervisors

claim: State law itself calls a supervisors district a beat
quote: Each supervisor of Supervisors Districts One and Two shall nominate and the board of supervisors shall appoint one (1) person from each

claim: The same section refers to each supervisor district as a beat
quote: beat for a one-year term

claim: Constables are elected by beat
quote: duly elected constables of any beat of any county

claim: The board may redraw supervisors districts by a three-fifths vote
quote: the board, by a three-fifths (3/5) vote of all members elected, may change the districts

claim: Each county has a sheriff, coroner, assessor, tax collector and surveyor, with four-year terms
quote: there shall be a sheriff, coroner, assessor, tax collector and surveyor for each county

claim: The Legislature may combine these county offices
quote: The Legislature may combine any one or more of said offices in any county or counties

claim: Every county has justice court judges (at least two) and constables
quote: A competent number of justice court judges and constables shall be chosen in each county in the manner provided by law, but not less than two (2) such judges in any county

claim: The number of justice court judges (two to five) follows county population
quote: In counties with a population, according to the latest federal decennial census, of thirty-five thousand (35,000) and less, there shall be two (2) justice court judges

claim: County home rule does not let a board of supervisors change county election procedures or create elective offices
quote: change the requirements, practices or procedures for county elections or establish any new elective office

claim: Counties have home rule over county affairs not covered by general law
quote: shall have the power to adopt any orders, resolutions or ordinances with respect to county affairs, property and finances, for which no specific provision has been made by general law

claim: Mississippi has 82 counties, each with its own section of Title 19, Chapter 1, ending with Yazoo County at § 19-1-163
quote: § 19-1-163. Yazoo County.

claim: Mississippi municipalities are cities, towns and villages
quote: in each city, town or village

claim: The Legislature charters cities and towns under general laws
quote: under which cities and towns may be chartered and their charters amended

claim: Code charter municipalities elect a mayor, aldermen, municipal judge, marshal or chief of police, tax collector and tax assessor
quote: The elective officers of all municipalities operating under a code charter shall be the mayor, the aldermen, municipal judge, the marshal or chief of police, the tax collector

claim: By ordinance, a code charter municipality may make every office except mayor and aldermen appointive
quote: to provide that all or any of such officers, except those of mayor and aldermen, shall be appointive

claim: Such an ordinance cannot be adopted within 90 days before a regular municipal election
quote: no such ordinance shall be adopted within ninety (90) days prior to any regular general election for the election of municipal officers

claim: Code charter municipalities under 10,000 have five aldermen, at large or four wards plus one at large
quote: in all municipalities having a population of less than ten thousand (10,000) according to the latest available federal census, there shall be five (5) aldermen

claim: Municipalities of 10,000 or more have seven aldermen, at large or six wards plus one at large
quote: there shall be seven (7) aldermen

claim: Every alderman, including ward aldermen, is selected by the whole town electorate
quote: All aldermen shall be selected by vote of the entire electorate of the municipality

claim: Ward versus at-large election of aldermen can be put to a vote on a 20% petition
quote: shall be determined by the vote of the majority of the qualified electors of the municipality voting in a special election called for that purpose

claim: A town of 500 or fewer may cut to three aldermen by a vote of its residents
quote: In any municipality having a population of five hundred (500) or less according to the latest available federal census, there may be three (3) aldermen

claim: The alderman count does not apply to special charter cities
quote: This section in no way affects the number of aldermen, councilmen, or commissioners of any city operating under a special charter

claim: Mayor-council municipalities elect a mayor and a council
quote: Each municipality operating under the mayor-council form of government shall be governed by an elected council and an elected mayor

claim: Mayor-council councils have five, seven or nine members, by ward or ward plus at large
quote: The council shall consist of five (5), seven (7) or nine (9) members

claim: Mayor-council officers are elected at the regular June municipal election for four-year terms
quote: shall be elected by the voters of the municipality at a regular municipal election held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June

claim: Municipal home rule does not let a city change municipal election procedures or create elective offices
quote: change the requirements, practices or procedures for municipal elections or establish any new elective office

claim: Municipalities have home rule over municipal affairs not inconsistent with state law
quote: shall have the power to adopt any orders, resolutions or ordinances with respect to such municipal affairs, property and finances
